item.title: See Tyler, The Creator's eccentric FC Barcelona kits for El Clásico
item.description: FC Barcelona's new kits are a little odd. The defending La Liga champions have partnered with Tyler, The Creator for the latest edition of their Spotify artist kit collaboration . Instead of just slapping a logo on a jersey, the entertainer, entrepreneur and founding member of Odd Future is the first artist to have full creative control of the capsule collection. To start, Tyler, The Creator put a gold block "GOLF" logo from his GOLF WANG brand on the front of FC Barcelona's red and blue striped home kit. Per usual for the artist collaboration, the jersey will be worn in the club's El Clásico match against Real Madrid. This year, Lamine Yamal and the men's team will wear it during the rivalry game on Oct. 25 at Camp Nou. The match will be the first Clásico fixture broadcast on ABC . The women's team will wear the kits a day prior in their match against Granada. Last year, FC Barcelona clinched the La Liga championship in El Clásico while wearing Olivia Rodrigo-branded kits . Other artists that have been featured in the Spotify kit collaboration include Karol G, Ed Sheeran, Travis Scott, Rosalía, Coldplay, The Rolling Stones and Drake. As with previous editions, there are 1,899 GOLF WANG jerseys available for purchase to commemorate the year Barcelona was established. From there, Tyler, The Creator created a merchandise collection that reflects his playful, renegade style. For one of the pieces, a white block "GOLF" logo sits on the front of a teal blue kit with a collar and a wavy pattern of "GG" and "Barca." There's also a dark brown leopard print longsleeve T-shirt with "Barca" in the blue color, and a varsity jacket in dark brown with the same design. A bright blue track jacket has the club's crest on one side and red and yellow stripes going down the arms. There's also T-shirts, hoodies, a water bottle, pin and sticker with a cartoon-like version of the crest and the words "GOLF" and "Barca" as well as a special edition blue leopard print soccer ball and brown scarf. View this post on Instagram The artist, born Tyler Okonma, also directed and starred in a promotional clip for the collaboration. He plays an executive who holds a larger-than-life tryout to join the club. The jerseys and soccer ball are featured in the comedic bit. And that's not all! Spotify will also host Copa De Golf, a night of music and culture on Oct. 24 in Barcelona. Odd Future member Taco will deejay a showcase of local artists. Tyler, The Creator previously worked with Pharrell on a whimsical Louis Vuitton collection that had colorful monograms and motifs of dogs and waffles. He also worked with F1 champion Lewis Hamilton for a merchandise collection ahead of the 2024 Las Vegas Grand Prix. They created a GOLF WANG and +44 capsule collection where, among the usual jacket and shirt offerings, there was a branded tire pressure gauge. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: See Tyler, The Creator's eccentric FC Barcelona kits for El Clásico

item.title: Canon-Mac football coach returns after second battle with cancer in five years
item.description: Canon-McMillian Head Coach returns after beating cancer a second time Football has been a part of Mike Evans’ life since before he can remember. “Last year was the first year I didn’t have a football season since I was like 10,” said Evans. The Canon-McMillian Head Coach was sidelined, battling cancer for the second time in five years. “I always thought I was coming back,” said Evans. “I don’t know what else to do. I can’t do anything else, so this is it. I coach football or I’m unemployed.” In February, after he was cleared by his doctors, Evans returned to the team. “He came back his first day in school in February and 12 of our players every lunch period were in his office just wanting to talk,” said quarterback Ty Jansma. In Evans’ absence, his close friend offensive coordinator Brian DeLallo stepped in as the interim head coach. “I don’t want to get emotional,” said Evans. “The guy really helped me out.” “It’s been a lot of fun coaching with him,” said DeLallo. “It’s like getting your best friend back. There aren’t enough words to describe Evans’ gratitude for DeLallo. Even when, against his wishes, the players put stickers on their helmets last season in support of their coach. “He said ‘I told you not to do that,’” said DeLallo. “I said ‘the kids overruled me. the kids wanted it, and that’s why we did that.” “Sometimes they don’t always see the tender, emotional side of me,” joked Evans. “But I was touched that they would do that.” The toughest team wins, Coach Evans’ favorite saying, is something they’ve embraced this season. His fight setting an example and providing his players with a heavy dose of perspective. “He gives us so much motivation because of how much he cares about us and how much he cares about the game,” said Jansma. “I don’t even have words for it.” But his impact on the team is far greater. “They love him like he’s a father figure,” said DeLallo. “To some of these kids he really is a father figure. To have him back with our program as a technician, as a master of scheme, as a motivator and as a friend to the kids, you can’t put a value on that.” And for Evans, who’s back on the sideline where he’s been practically his entire life, he can’t help but stop for a minute, and be filled with gratitude. “One of the motivations was to come back,” said Evans. “I mean obviously it was to live, but this is living.” Download the FREE WPXI News app for breaking news alerts. item.title: Tricolor hold final training session before facing Vasco da Gama
item.description: Tricolor hold final training session before facing Vasco da Gama On Friday afternoon (16), at the Barra Funda training center, the Tricolor held their final training session before facing Vasco da Gama this Saturday (17), at 9 p.m., at MorumBIS, in the 31st round of the Brazilian Championship. The final day of preparations began with the coaching staff showing the players a video in the auditorium. Shortly afterward, out on the pitch, the fitness coaches led the warm-up. Head coach Dorival Júnior and his assistants then oversaw tactical drills, working on build-up play and attacking and defensive set pieces. Forwards Luciano and Calleri, who have recovered from a right adductor injury and left thigh pain, respectively, trained with the squad. Forward Ferreira, who is working his way back from a right adductor injury, took part in some of the drills with his teammates and did additional work with the fitness staff. Against Vasco da Gama, the Tricolor will look to maintain their recent strong record at MorumBIS in the Brasileirão. São Paulo have won four of their last five home games in the competition: against Red Bull Bragantino (2–1), Atlético Mineiro (2–0), Internacional (1–0) and Vitória (2–1). item.title: Can Evan Bouchard Keep Up His Hot Pace?
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Few players have been as important to the Edmonton Oilers’ success in recent seasons as Evan Bouchard. item.description: Michael C. Johnson-Imagn Images Thomas Castellanos gets massive update for Texas Tech-Arizona State clash appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Nothing should surprise Texas Tech football fans at this point. The Red Raiders have dealt with plenty of injunctions and eligibility controversy , but the latest development is working in their favor. Thomas Castellanos has been granted a temporary injunction , per On3’s Pete Nakos, allowing him to rejoin the squad. The 23-year-old quarterback is one of many players who have pursued a fifth-year of eligibility this season, a privilege the NCAA is extending to everyone who enrolled after the 2022 freshmen class. Athletes have unsurprisingly flocked to courtrooms to fight the ruling, but the opposition has been steady and fierce. Castellanos, who operates primarily as a rusher for Texas Tech in special packages, has endured his share of ups and downs during this legal process. Originally permitted to play, the mobile signal-caller saw his injunction get reversed by a panel of judges in Kentucky and was therefore ineligible to compete in an Oct. 3 win over Colorado. He is back in action for the moment, however. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Will Hammond remains the team’s No. 1 passing QB, but head coach Joey McGuire obviously values the elusiveness Castellanos can bring. The former UCF, Boston College and Florida State QB has completed 2-of-4 passes for 35 yards and two touchdowns, while rushing for 44 yards and two more TDs. It remains to be seen what role he will occupy in Saturday afternoon’s home matchup against Arizona State, but the Red Raiders will at least have options Eligibility debates will hopefully cease to exist starting next season, but for now, Thomas Castellanos and other fifth-year seekers will continue to operate with a chip on their shoulder. Texas Tech and Arizona State square off at 3:30 p.m. ET in Lubbock. item.title: Buccaneers coach reveals what makes Aaron Rodgers so hard to beat
item.description: Buccaneers coach reveals what makes Aaron Rodgers so hard to beat originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Going up against MVP-winning quarterback Aaron Rodgers tends to give a lot of head coaches and teams an "oh, no" feeling. Even though Rodgers is now in his 40s and some would argue he's past his prime, he's a veteran player who still knows how to win. It's almost like going up against a coach on the field. The Pittsburgh Steelers and Tampa Bay Buccaneers play on Sunday in Week 6 of the NFL season. It's a road game for the Steelers, and it's also a win the Buccaneers need. Heading into the game, the Steelers are 3-2 and the Buccaneers are 1-4, so both teams could use a pick-me-up with a solid win. Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles has faced Rodgers before. He's 2-2 against the quarterback as a coach and defensive coordinator, so he knows what it's like to go up against Rodgers. Todd Bowles explains why Aaron Rodgers is such a 'nightmare' for opposing defenses ESPN has unleashed its Week 6 preview ahead of the weekend of games , and in it, reporter Jenna Laine shares the Buccaneers' thoughts about this matchup. "It's a nightmare game-planning against him," Bowles said of going up against Rodgers, per Laine. "He's difficult because he's extremely intelligent... He's extremely accurate with the football, and he can dissect things before the play even happens." Laine adds that "Bowles has been relatively successful using disguises against him. Rodgers has a career raw QBR of 33.9 against Bowles when he uses disguised coverage -- which ranks 40th among all QBs against Bowles teams. Rodgers' QBR is 54.6 against disguised coverages as a whole." So, the Buccaneers can certainly win this game. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will once again get the start at quarterback with Baker Mayfield out. But anything is possible because this is the NFL. item.title: NY Yankees risk wasting a starter to patch their bullpen
item.description: Oct 5, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; New York Yankees pitcher Ryan Weathers (40) pitches against the Tampa Bay Rays during the seventh inning in game two of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A projected rotation can look full in October and look very different by the first week of April. The Yankees should remember that before deciding Ryan Weathers is a convenient way to fill their bullpen. Matthew Schmidt raised the possibility of using Weathers in relief in a Thursday Roundtable Sports offseason column . It is a reasonable proposal to examine, not an announced Yankees plan. A left-hander with his ability could help in that assignment. The cost is the starting work New York would be asking somebody else to provide. Weathers already gave the Yankees useful innings Weathers made 25 regular-season starts and threw 137 1/3 innings with a 3.60 ERA. He struck out 143 and walked 38. A pitcher who supplied that workload shouldn’t be moved permanently because six names fit neatly onto an offseason depth chart. Oct 3, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; New York Yankees pitcher Ryan Weathers (40) delivers a pitch in the sixth inning in game one of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs against the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Carlos Rodon and Will Warren are all still on the current roster. Add Weathers and there are six recognizable starting options. That doesn’t establish six healthy pitchers ready to handle every assignment for an entire season, or settle which five should get the opening jobs. I wouldn’t convert him to a permanent reliever before that surplus actually exists. Keep him prepared to start, let the winter’s other decisions develop and assess the available innings when the team has more information. Reversing a relief assignment after a rotation injury is possible, but rebuilding a workload isn’t as simple as changing the label next to his name. The bullpen argument deserves a fair hearing There is an appealing version of the idea. In a shorter assignment, a starter can attack hitters without planning for several trips through the order. A multi-inning left-hander also gives a manager more ways to finish a game than a pitcher restricted to one narrow matchup. 0 What do you think? Post a comment. None of that guarantees Weathers would become a dominant reliever. His starter numbers don’t establish how his command, recovery or stuff would respond to a different schedule. New York would be making a projection, not exchanging 137 innings of proven starting work for an equally proven late-game outcome. The sensible alternative is to leave relief available as a situational assignment. If the rotation is healthy, another starter has earned the place and a particular stretch calls for extra bullpen length

item.description: Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images, Big Noon Kickoff Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy has been taking plenty of shots at Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day this week ahead of the team’s top-five showdown with the Indiana Hoosiers on Saturday, and Ohio State fans have not been happy about it. Now, Portnoy has responded to the backlash, calling Buckeyes fans “delusional” and “sensitive” and claiming that the fan base has an unhealthy obsession with him. ‘Ryan Day was born on third base’ As a Michigan alum, Portnoy has never been shy about criticizing Day over the years, but the feud with Ohio State has gotten more personal since he was removed from Fox’s Big Noon Kickoff pregame show earlier this month. He blamed Day and the Buckeyes for the decision, writing in a post on X that Ohio State “[complained] and moaned to the Big 10 and threatened Fox till they had no choice” and referring to the coach as “Cryin Ryan.” While making picks for Saturday’s game earlier this week, Portnoy took things a step further , arguing that Indiana’s Curt Cignetti is a much better coach than Day. “If this game is close coming down in the fourth quarter, Cignetti is about 100x the game coach that Ryan Day is,” Portnoy said while previewing the game between Indiana and Ohio State. “Cignetti is clearly a superstar coach, and it doesn’t matter where he went. Ryan Day would be unsuccessful at any program other than Ohio State. He was given a cupboard full of superstars. He could never build a program. He could never do what Cignetti did.” Portnoy went on to echo former Michigan head coach Jim Harbaugh’s famous jab at Day. “Ryan Day was born on third base,” he said. “Like, anybody here could coach that team to 10, 11 wins.” ‘Fetish city’ Needless to say, Ohio State fans were not too thrilled by Portnoy’s comments, but he wasn’t backing down. In a social media post on Friday, Portnoy absolutely blasted Ohio State fans, calling them “delusional and insane and sensitive” as he suggested they have a “fetish” for him. “I love how delusional and insane and sensitive and some would say stupid Ohio Stare fans are. Im one of the longest running college football analysts in the country. Literally. They are mad I talked about Ohio State vs Indiana this week (biggest game of the weekend) and said Indiana has a coaching advantage which they clearly do with Cignetti > Day. They act like I am biased against them when I give good, clean fair takes. I swear Ohio State has a Dave Portnoy fetish. They can’t stay out of mentions and they can’t stop obsessing over me. Fetish city,” Portnoy wrote in a post on X . Indiana is a 3.5-point home underdog in Saturday’s game, which kicks off at noon ET on Fox. Portnoy’s been pretty vocal about his pick, so it’s safe to say that if the Buckeyes win, Ohio State fans are surely going to let the Barstool Sports founder hear about it. item.title: USC President Addresses Lincoln Riley’s Future Amid $70 Million Buyout Talk
item.description: USC has a new president, Beong-Soo Kim, and he has already made a definitive statement on the future of head coach Lincoln Riley. After the loss to Oregon this season and other disappointing results during his tenure, Riley is on the hot seat, at least with fans. Will USC pay the Lincoln Riley buyout To move on from Riley, USC would need to pay a $70 million buyout. In an LA Times profile, Kim declined to say whether USC could or would pay such a large buyout. “We’re not thinking about that,” Kim said in his LA Times story. “We are laser focused on the next game, and then the game after that.” In 2021, Lincoln Riley signed a 10-year, $110 million deal, and he is now halfway through it without a College Football Playoff appearance. Sep 26, 2026; Los Angeles, California, USA; USC Trojans head coach Lincoln Riley walks off the field after the game against the Oregon Ducks at United Airlines Field at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Additionally, while the offense has been electric, Riley has failed to solve the defensive issues that limit the team just about every season. Where USC’s season stands This season, USC is 6-1, boosted somewhat by a weak non-conference schedule. They are 3-1 in Big Ten play, though the hardest part of their schedule still remains. item.title: Deepti Sharma, debutant Niki Prasad rescue India after top-order collapse against Zimbabwe
item.description: Experienced Deepti Sharma and debutant Niki Prasad helped India recover from a top-order collapse to secure a four-wicket win over Zimbabwe in the first T20I in Raipur on Friday. India had to work harder than expected while chasing a target of 115, but recovered from losing four wickets for just 19 runs to reach the target with 4.2 overs to spare. Smriti Mandhana began her first match as India's full-time T20I captain with a couple of boundaries, but her dismissal triggered a collapse that left India struggling at 19 for 4 in the fourth over. Mandhana fell for one in the second over, followed by Anushka Sharma. Harmanpreet Kaur's wicket left India at 19 for 3 before Shafali Verma was dismissed at the same score, leaving the hosts in trouble inside the powerplay. Nyasha Gwanzura played a key role in the collapse, dismissing Mandhana, Anushka and Shafali with her offspin, while Michelle Mavunga sent Harmanpreet back to the pavilion. Zimbabwe, who had lost all 18 of their T20Is this year, suddenly had a chance to pull off an upset. However, Deepti and debutant Niki had other plans. Deepti scored 49 off 37 balls, while Niki made 39 off 35 as the pair put together an 82-run partnership for the fifth wicket to bring India back into the contest and put them on course for victory. Niki eventually sealed the win with a boundary, with India reaching the target with 4.2 overs to spare. It was a challenging start to her international career, with the youngster walking in when India were in deep trouble before helping guide them to victory. — BCCIWomen (@BCCIWomen) Earlier, Zimbabwe had reached 60 for 1 after 10 overs, with Kelis Ndhlovu looking comfortable at the crease. India’s bowlers then kept the scoring in check through the middle overs. World No. 1 N Shree Charani finished with figures of 1 for 14, while Nandani Sharma took two wickets in the final over to end with 2 for 11. Ndhlovu scored 42, while Sharne Mayers added an unbeaten 43 to help Zimbabwe finish at 114 for 5.

item.title: Israel Adesanya’s UFC future hinges on Shara Magomedov fight
item.description: One of the greatest fighters of the modern era has his next fight set. Former UFC middleweight champion Israel Adesanya is booked to headline a Fight Night event in Saudi Arabia against dynamic striker and fan favorite Shara Magomedov. Uncrowned’s Ariel Helwani confirmed the fight during a live stream of “The Ariel Helwani Show” on YouTube. MORE: Alexander Volkanovski eyes UFC lightweight title fight against Justin Gaethje In terms of competition level, this is a massive step down for Adesanya. Shara Bullet doesn’t have any really good wins. All of Shara’s wins are against older fighters past their prime or prospects matched with him to make him look good. Shara’s last fight was a unanimous-decision win over Michel Pereira, who has since lost four of his last five fights. Before that, Shara defeated Marc-Andre Barriault, who has also now lost four of his last five fights. Now fighting for the second time in 2026, Israel Adesanya has his best chance in years to win. Shara isn’t going to engage in any grappling. While Shara does have impressive footwork and versatility as a striker, Adesanya built a career off of those skills. MORE: Paddy Pimblett offers update on UFC return, eyes Ilia Topuria fight Adesanya has lost four straight, but unlike Shara’s other opponents, he’s lost to the best. With losses to Sean Strickland, Dricus Du Plessis, Nassourdine Imavov, and Joe Pyfer, Adesanya is clearly no longer amongst the elite at 185 pounds. That said, neither is Shara Magomedov, so this fight will answer one big question. Israel Adesanya is fighting to prove he’s still UFC caliber Sep 9, 2023; Sydney, NSW, AUSTRALIA; Israel Adesanya reacts during his fight with Sean Strickland. Mandatory Credit: Jasmin Frank-USA TODAY Sports Credit: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect (Reuters) A loss for Adesanya here won’t come with the excuse that he got beat by one of the best in the world. Shara Bullet is not that; he’s fun, but he’s not elite. This would be a fifth loss in a row. At 37, why would Adesanya keep going, especially if each loss makes the next fights less significant? item.description: No. 9 Jasper and Memorial boys tennis both saw their season come to an end in the IHSAA state quarterfinals on Friday, October 16. Originally expected to be played at North Central in Indianapolis, the Wildcats and Tigers had their postseason matches moved indoors due to weather. The matches were played at the UIndy Tennis Center. More: Two teams representing SW Indiana in IHSAA boys tennis state finals Jasper loses top-10 battle to Center Grove Jasper lost its match to No. 3 Center Grove 5-0. No. 2 singles Nicolas Aguilera and No. 3 singles Michael Braun pushed their respective matches to a third set but were unable to come away with points. It was a return to the state finals for the Wildcats after missing out on the trip to Indianapolis last season. Coach Scott Yarbrough looks back on not just his group’s performance against Center Grove, but the entirety of the season, with a great appreciation of what was accomplished. “I thought our team this year did a nice job of continually improving and getting better each day,” Yarbrough said. "I loved the way we battled today. Proud of what these boys accomplished and proud of those 7 seniors and the four years they gave to our program.” Elliott Rolwing (No. 1 singles), Aguilera and Collin Werner (No. 1 doubles) are the seniors departing from Jasper’s starting lineup. Memorial pushes Delta Memorial lost its match to No. 6 Delta 4-1. No. 3 singles Ty Jackson won his match (6-3, 0-6, 6-4), earning the Tigers their lone point. “Ty’s a great fighter,” Memorial coach Will Hays said. “Ty’s been a really big part of our postseason. He’s only a sophomore, so it’s going to be really exciting to see him grow.” No. 2 doubles Graham Miller and Andon Baker pushed their match to a third set before losing the tiebreaker 10-7. Hays was proud of the way his team competed throughout the match. Departing the program is No. 1 singles Zach Woodyard and its No. 1 doubles duo of Kenneth Dilger and Porter Wil. Hays said he valued the trio’s leadership and reliability this season. Just like Jasper, Memorial made its return to the state finals after a one-year absence. This was accomplished in Will Hays’ first season coaching the group. Memorial was an unranked team for the entirety of this season. Hays reflects on the campaign with an appreciation of his group’s effort and ability to be coached. “This team was really good at working hard when they were pushed,” Hays said. “I think they needed a coach like me to push them a little bit. item.title: Brewers' Abner Uribe visits Oak Creek store to buy hard-to-find camera
item.description: This Milwaukee Brewers pitcher is equally at home releasing a pitch and releasing the shutter on a camera. Reliever Abner Uribe recently stopped in at Impulse, 7965 S. Main St., a camera store in Oak Creek . Impulse co-owner Travis Garski said he got a phone call out of nowhere from a public relations representative for Uribe. The caller said his client was looking for a Canon PowerShot G7X Mark III , a camera Garski said is nearly impossible to keep in stock. Retail for the compact camera, which came out in 2019, is $879.99, but Garski said many third-party resellers inflate the price due to its popularity. When asked why it was popular, Garski said he didn’t know exactly, other than a lot of social media influence. Uribe wanted one quickly, Garski said, guessing he wanted to use it to document this historic run for the Brewers. “I’m assuming he wanted something better than his phone that he can carry in his pocket,” Garski said. Luckily Garski was able to get a hold of one through his contacts, and it only took about a week from call to camera in hand for Uribe, who visited Impulse around 6 p.m. Oct. 9, two days after the Brewers defeated the San Diego Padres 3-1 to win the National League Division series. More: A new camera store and studio opening in Oak Creek is raffling $7K in gear its opening day Garski said since the pitcher popped into the store, he’s been watching more baseball, often having a game on one of the wall-mounted televisions at Impulse. “He’s really good,” Garski said of Uribe on the mound. “He’s got a lot of energy.” When he was in the shop, however, Garski said the 26-year-old reliever was very quiet and reserved. “Maybe he was just exhausted,” Garski said. Brewers headed to the World Series for the first time in 44 years The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-4 on Oct. 15 , propelling the team to the World Series for the first time since 1982. Garski said he’s proud of the Brewers for getting to the Fall Classic and is excited to watch the games. He said Wisconsin pushes out some good players in all sports. As a thank you, Garski said Uribe's representative is gifting the store four tickets for a Brewers game next year along with passes allowing them to go on the field before the game – and bring their cameras. Impulse has an engraving machine and Garski said he's invited Uribe back to the store to get the camera engraved, maybe even with champion wording if the Brewers win the World Series. Williams’ comments regarding the media follow her rise to recognition as one of the WNBA’s top two-way players. While the Valkyries are generally known for and take pride in their depth instead of leaning on a true superstar, Williams has taken her game to new heights in the postseason, averaging 22.7 points, 4.8 rebounds, and four assists per game, while shooting 40.5% from three. She was named to her second consecutive All-Star team this season and finished runner-up in the Defensive Player of the Year voting, underscoring her increased media recognition. The 2025-26 Ted Lindsay Award finalist played in all 82 games last year, and an early preview of life without Celebrini this season wasn’t pretty. Hopefully for the Sharks, it won’t be a reality they have to experience again anytime soon. Smith, Askarov Marred by Inconsistent Play As presumably long-term franchise pillars, the ceilings for Smith and goaltender Yaroslav Askarov are limitless. And that’s what makes their erratic play so frustrating. Smith made a statement on opening night, appearing to have taken a drastic jump in Year 3. Celebrini’s willingness to battle for the puck may finally be rubbing off on his roommate, as Smith’s physicality, forechecking and play along the boards were truly eye-opening and an encouraging sign. View this post on Instagram His offensive gifts were on full display, but he was also more focused and engaged away from the puck. But in the matchups since, much like last season, Smith has had extended stretches where he leaves minimal imprints on games, disappearing for shifts and periods on end, playing like an average forward instead of the emerging star he could be. In the opener versus Florida, he looked timid and nervous. But once he got over the first-game jitters, Stenberg has picked up confidence, and his play has followed. Stenberg’s offensive instincts are top-notch for a player at any age, let alone 19. His neutral zone play is also surprisingly sharp for a rookie. Head coach Ryan Warsofsky already trusts Stenberg to garner a spot on the top power-play unit and make the right decisions in 3-on-3 overtime scenarios — a testament to his maturity and elite hockey IQ. The Swedish winger notched his first career point against the Kings in his second game, finding Toffoli parked net front on a sweet pass. item.title: Brennan Poole Joins Jordan Anderson Racing for 2027 NASCAR Season
item.description: Photo by: Mike Watters Poole Lands Full Time Ride With Jordan Anderson Racing Brennan Poole has found his next home in NASCAR, announcing Friday that he will drive full time for Jordan Anderson Racing Bommarito Autosport in the 2027 NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series season. Poole will take over the team’s No. 31 Chevrolet, marking a new chapter in his career after three seasons with Alpha Prime Racing. The announcement was made at Phoenix Raceway as the O’Reilly Auto Parts Series continues its championship battle. Poole’s move gives him an opportunity to compete with a new organization while continuing his career in NASCAR’s second tier national series. A New Opportunity for a NASCAR Veteran Poole brings plenty of experience to Jordan Anderson Racing. The Texas native has made more than 200 career starts in the O’Reilly Auto Parts Series and has also competed in the NASCAR Cup Series and Craftsman Truck Series. His best season in the O’Reilly Series standings came in 2017, when he finished sixth overall. Throughout his career, Poole has earned a reputation for making the most of his equipment and competing consistently against experienced drivers. During his three-year run with Alpha Prime Racing, Poole helped the organization record several strong finishes. He has earned three top five finishes and 11 top 10 results with the team, according to reports covering his move. Poole announced earlier this week that he would leave Alpha Prime Racing after the 2026 season. The organization had hoped to retain him as it prepares for a new chapter with Ford, but Poole ultimately decided to pursue a different opportunity. A Reunion More Than 20 Years in the Making The move carries a personal connection for Poole and team president Jordan Anderson. The two first competed against each other in Legends cars in 2004, beginning a relationship that has continued throughout their racing careers. Anderson expressed excitement about finally working alongside Poole after years of competing against him. He praised Poole’s ability to maximize his equipment, communicate with crew members and help develop a competitive race team. Poole also welcomed the opportunity, pointing to Jordan Anderson Racing’s strong Chevrolet relationship and the team’s investment in building a winning organization. His existing sponsors, including Macc Door Systems, Toxic Waste Candy, and CW & Sons and Clarks Directional Boring, are expected to continue supporting him in 2027. Looking Ahead to 2027 Poole will join Daniel Dye as a full-time driver for Jordan Anderson Racing next season. The team’s plans for its No. 27 entry have not yet been finalized. For Poole, the goal will be turning this new opportunity into stronger results and a chance to climb the championship standings. With an established team, continued sponsorship support and a familiar manufacturer, he will enter 2027 looking to take another step forward in his NASCAR career.

Elvis Presley’s high baritone and Andy Williams’ tenor on the public address system marked a different type of occasion. Bournemouth have come a significant distance. “Minus 17 to European dreams” read a banner in the Steve Fletcher stand, marking the journey from the foot of the Football League to becoming a model, continental club. Milan visit next week, an occasion to further broaden the smile of Bill Foley, Bournemouth’s financier present in the posh seats. “A long time coming,” said Bournemouth’s long-serving captain, Adam Smith. “The fans were up for it, the players were up for it.” Continue reading...

item.title: Chelsea are the Premier League’s most fun team but is it sustainable?
item.description: Xabi Alonso’s side are scoring and conceding at a remarkable rate. Goals arrive in abundance, leads are established before spectators have settled into their seats and clean sheets have become an alien concept. Xabi Alonso has transformed Chelsea into one of the Premier League’s most thrilling spectacles. They have scored 15 goals and conceded 13. That’s 4.7 goals per game in six matches. Chelsea are a neutral’s dream, but is it sustainable? They have scored 15 goals from an expected goals total of just 8.4, an over-performance of 6.6. Their 18.3% conversion rate is second only to Manchester City’s 19.1%, while eight of their 15 goals have come from shots with xG below 0.13. It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Christian Pulisic is no longer a focal point for the US or Milan – and that’s OK
item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. Last year, he was involved in US friendlies against Ecuador and Australia. But this year, with Fifa having folded the October window into September, Pulisic didn’t have the chance. On Sunday, his pre-match music was O Generosa, the Serie A anthem, which he observed with a soft smile. Mark Twain’s first visit to Italy left him describing the country as “a vast museum of magnificence and misery”, and it’s a fitting summary of Pulisic’s three-plus years with Milan. The magnificence: 43 goals and 25 assists in 138 appearances. The misery: just one trophy since he arrived in July 2023, a 2025 Supercoppa Italia held in Saudi Arabia. Continue reading...

item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘I wanted to depart in the best way possible’: Kieran McKenna on Ipswich exit and future plans
item.description: In an exclusive interview, former Ipswich manager talks of his lasting affection for the club, savouring time out with family and friends and ideas for his next move It was on the Portman Road pitch, bathed in bright early May light while immersed in the relief and joy of a third promotion in five years, that Kieran McKenna realised the moment was right. The thought had flickered earlier in the season that this might be his final campaign at Ipswich, only to be pushed into the subconscious by the Championship’s remorseless grind. “But standing out there, I felt this was probably time,” he says of those moments after QPR had been swept aside and a return to the Premier League assured. “Another big victory, a full stadium, in front of my family and the fans. It was an amazing way to go out on a high.” Five months later McKenna has no regrets about electing to cut things short while the going was so good. The golf bag lying outside his garage speaks of a man enjoying the break and, more pertinently, of something bigger. His son has recently become interested in the sport and sharing those moments with loved ones, whether out on the greens or spending part of the summer travelling along the East Anglian coastline in a camper van, were among the biggest reasons to pause a soaring career. At 40, McKenna had spent two decades immersed in coaching; it was time to appreciate life’s essentials while continuing professional development at his own speed. Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
